title: Persistent Storage for Regional Inventory Analytics
business: A regional logistics firm managing high-frequency inventory tracking databases that require consistent block-level storage performance.
problem: The firm faces data loss risks during instance termination because their current ephemeral storage is wiped when the virtual machine shuts down, preventing long-term state retention for their analytics engine.
solution: Amazon EBS provides persistent block-level storage volumes that remain independent of the lifecycle of an EC2 instance, allowing the firm to detach and reattach volumes to different instances as needed to maintain data continuity.
steps: Provision an Amazon EBS volume in the same Availability Zone as the target EC2 instance.
Attach the EBS volume to the EC2 instance using the AWS Management Console or CLI.
Format the volume with a file system like ext4 or XFS within the operating system.
Mount the volume to a specific directory to begin writing persistent data.
Create periodic snapshots of the volume to ensure point-in-time recovery capability.
outcome: The firm achieves reliable data persistence where inventory records survive instance restarts or failures, ensuring that analytics workloads can resume immediately without manual data restoration.
limitation: An EBS volume is restricted to a single Availability Zone, meaning it cannot be attached to instances in different zones simultaneously; this is verified by checking the volume's availability zone attribute in the AWS console.
